14-## Project overview
15-
16:Web app: turns a book's text into character portraits and one chapter illustration via the Gemini API. Five user-driven steps, run one at a time by the user: Style → Characters → Portraits → Chapters → Illustrations. Scope is bounded on purpose — max 2 adult characters, max 1 chapter, enforced server-side.
17-
18-Two modes, chosen up front and **locked when Style runs**: **Auto** (the server picks the top characters/scene — the original behaviour) or **Selection** (the user picks which characters/chapter to illustrate from a model-proposed candidate pool). A **no-content guard** stops non-book / too-short text (no characters or chapters found → delete and start over).
19-
20-## Tech stack
21-
22-- **Next.js** — full-stack (frontend + API route handlers), one framework for both. Chosen because the scope is bounded; a single framework is enough, no separate frontend/backend services.
23:- **Gemini API** — text model + Nano Banana image model, via the Interactions API (chained by `previous_interaction_id`) with File API upload for the book. JS SDK available (Next.js is JS); REST is the fallback. Model IDs: TBD.
24-- **Storage** — JSON files on disk (no DB). One file per entity type: `data/projects.json`, `data/users.json`; load → mutate object → serialize back (demo's pattern, swapped off localStorage to server disk). Lock on the file + atomic temp-write/rename. Images and book text are separate files under `data/`, referenced by path, served through our own API. See `DECISIONS.md`.
25-
26:## Gemini API rules
27-
28:- **Backend only.** Every Gemini call happens server-side. Never call Gemini from the client — protects the key and keeps the single-call guard in one place.
29:- **Official SDK.** Use the official Gemini SDK (JS, since Next.js is JS), not hand-rolled REST unless the SDK lacks an endpoint we need.
30-- **Send the book once, reuse the result.** Upload the book once (File API) and chain interactions by id (`previous_interaction_id`). Never re-send the full book text on later steps.
31:- **No auto-retry.** Never retry a failed Gemini call in a loop. Retries are user-triggered only.
32:- **Key in env var**, never committed. Ship `.env.example`.
33-- **Caps enforced server-side.** A finished project draws at most **2** character portraits + **1** chapter illustration — the hard, cost-bounding cap on *images* (each image is a paid request). In **Selection** mode the text step may propose a larger candidate *pool* (`CHARACTER_POOL` / `CHAPTER_POOL`, text-only and cheap) to pick from; **Auto** asks for only the capped count. Either way the backend caps the drawn images (`resolveSelection` slices to `MAX_CHARACTERS` / `MAX_CHAPTERS`) — never rely on the UI. The image caps are fixed literals, not tunables.
34-- **No-content guard.** If the text yields no characters/chapters, the step fails with a "delete this project / start a new one" message — there is no in-project recovery (you can't conjure characters a text lacks). Plus a length pre-check at project creation.
35-
36-## Commands
37-
38-> One command starts the stack, one runs the tests (§5.5). No Docker.
39-
40:- One-command wrappers (bash; Git Bash on Windows): `./start.sh` · `./test.sh` (each runs `npm install` first; `start.sh` also creates `.env` from `.env.example` on first run, never overwriting an existing one)
41-- Start: `npm run dev` (after `npm install`) · Test: `npm test`
42-- Build: `npm run build` · Lint: `npm run lint`
43-
44-## Code style
45-
--
50-- **Organized & reusable** — structured folder, code, clear module boundaries, factor shared logic into reusable helpers instead of copy-paste.
51-- **Least code, same result** — reach for the smallest solution that fully does the task. No abstractions for features we aren't shipping. Right-sized over clever.
52:- **Optimize** — remove dead code and needless work; keep hot paths (Gemini calls, polling, file I/O) lean. Optimize for clarity first, then cost.
53-
54-## Testing
55-
56-Kept simple and targeted — 3-day scope, no over-testing. No E2E.
57-
58-- **Layers**
59-  - **Unit (backend)** — pipeline logic: step-order guard, no-duplicate (running step returns in-flight), retry (failed step retryable, others untouched), stuck recovery (running+stale → retryable), caps (>2 chars / >1 chapter refused).
60:  - **Integration (backend)** — happy-path run through all 5 steps with a **mocked Gemini** (no quota, no key, deterministic).
61-  - **Component (frontend)** — key states only: error+retry, empty list, in-progress naming the step.
62:- **Tools** — Vitest (runner for unit + integration), React Testing Library (components), Gemini SDK mocked in all tests.
63-- **TDD leash** — test-first on backend pipeline logic (pins behavior before AI writes code); test-after on frontend states.
64-- **Deliverables** — `TESTING.md` (what we test, what we skip, why) + a real test-run report.
65-
66-## Repo etiquette

content.text:
I couldn't fully fix this. The key is missing or empty in your `.env`, and I can't fix that part for you.

- **What I changed:** `scripts/check-env.mjs` parsed `.env` by hand with `split('\n')` and `split('=')`. That breaks on CRLF line endings, an `export ` prefix, quoted values, surrounding whitespace, and a BOM. I replaced it with Node's built-in `util.parseEnv`, which handles all of those.
- **What I found:** `npm run dev` still prints `GEMINI_API_KEY is missing` with the robust parser. So the problem isn't formatting. `.env` has no non-empty `GEMINI_API_KEY` entry. The checker reads it from `./.env` in the current directory, so a file in another checkout won't count.
- **Why I stopped:** The project policy gate blocks me from reading `.env`, so I couldn't see why. I didn't try to get around it.

Check these in `.env` yourself:
- The line is exactly `GEMINI_API_KEY=<your key>`, with the name spelled correctly and a value after the `=`. It's probably still the empty placeholder copied from `.env.example`.
- The line isn't commented out with `#`.

After that, `npm run dev` should print `ready on http://localhost:3000`. If it still fails, tell me what the line looks like with the value masked, and I'll keep digging.

The `parseEnv` change is only in the working tree. I haven't committed it.
